source_behavior.summary: SiteOperationsMaintenance exposes a read-only Operation history navigation control alongside the distinct Refresh and Operations hub controls.
source_behavior.navigation: The canonical control navigates from either maintenance route alias to /site-operations.
source_behavior.scope_boundary: Refresh, Operations hub, cleanup preview, cleanup confirmation and cleanup execution are separate canonical operations and are not claimed by this closure.
source_behavior.read_semantics: Opening Operation history performs navigation only and does not mutate operation-history persistence or invoke WordPress, provider, queue, payment, email, DNS, approval or execution behavior.

laravel_adaptation.tenant_derivation: Both existing maintenance controllers validate the route tenant against TenantContext and pass only the authoritative active tenant slug to the views; Blade resolves the existing named history route from that slug.
laravel_adaptation.permission_alignment: Both source maintenance reads and the existing history target require execution.view, so an authorized maintenance reader cannot receive a navigation capability broader than the source boundary.

tenant_and_security_contract.active_tenant_source: TenantContext established by auth + tenant.context and rechecked by the maintenance controllers
tenant_and_security_contract.history_url_source: named canonical.workspace.site-operations route using the already-validated active tenant slug
tenant_and_security_contract.cross_tenant_result: 404 for both source aliases and the destination when an Alpha member attempts a Beta path
tenant_and_security_contract.identifier_minimization: The control contains only the trusted tenant slug and no site, history-record, credential, provider, execution, approval or arbitrary return-URL identifier.
tenant_and_security_contract.external_runtime: Navigation-only operation; no live WordPress, AI-provider, email, payment, DNS or production mutation evidence is required.

assertions: exact canonical operation identity, source aliases, visible-control fingerprint, read-only flag and tenant ownership
both real maintenance aliases render the exact canonical marker and tenant-scoped history destination
destination is the existing named canonical.workspace.site-operations GET route and retains execution.view with auth and tenant.context
guest requests redirect to login and a tenant member without execution.view receives 403 on source and target
foreign-tenant source and target paths fail closed with 404
opening both source aliases and the history target does not change operation-history persistence

terminality.reason: Both already-real maintenance aliases now expose the canonical tenant-scoped Operation history navigation with exact provenance and deterministic authorization, tenant-isolation and read-only coverage. Generator-controlled terminal credit remains contingent on this pushed evidence snapshot and repository CI.
